messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx and latency on embeddings and rerank in us-west-2. triggered at 2026-03-15T14:30:01Z. Paging @maya_oncall :rotating_light:

maya_oncall: ack. checking dashboards now. any signs of infra or a bad deploy?

devon: deployment check negative. no new prod deploys in last hour. traffic profile shows sudden surge on /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank from a small set of keys. chat endpoints ("/v1/chat/*") unaffected.

sam: logs show increased 502s coming from model backend timeouts during large batch rerank calls. rerank p95 CPU spikes to >95% on a few nodes.

maya_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) immediately lower per-route quotas for embeddings and rerank, 2) enable per-key hard throttles for the noisy keys, 3) temporarily disable synchronous heavy_rerank path, 4) monitor metrics for 10m and escalate if no improvement. devon, can you push route limits and feature flag?

devon: applying route limits via admin CLI for auditable history. commands: ```
# set conservative limits for region to prevent cascading failures
rictl route update --route "/v1/embeddings" --region us-west-2 --limit 500req/s --burst 250
rictl route update --route "/v1/rerank" --region us-west-2 --limit 60req/s --burst 40
```

ops-runbook-bot: Action logged: route_quota_change by devon at 2026-03-15T14:31:12Z. prev embeddings: 2500req/s. new: 500req/s. prev rerank: 300req/s. new: 60req/s.

maya_oncall: good. sending DM with top offending API keys to @devon for per-key throttles.

devon: throttling top offenders >1200req/min to hard caps: ```
rictl keys throttle --key-id key_77y --limit 45req/s --enforcement hard
rictl keys throttle --key-id key_9xz --limit 30req/s --enforcement hard
```

eng-release-bot: Feature flag toggle request queued by devon. Change: heavy_rerank_sync -> disabled in us-west-2.

devon: flipping feature flag now: ```
flagsctl set heavy_rerank_sync false --env prod --region us-west-2 --reason "mitigation for CPU/backpressure"
```

ops-runbook-bot: Action logged: feature_flag_changed by devon at 2026-03-15T14:33:07Z. heavy_rerank_sync=false (us-west-2).

sam: metrics after changes: embeddings p95 dropped from ~1.1s to ~420ms in 4 minutes, error rate dropped from 16% to 2.8%. rerank CPU normalized on previously impacted nodes.

liz: can we also set a temporary per-route quota differential: keep chat higher than embeddings and rerank. many customers rely primarily on chat.

maya_oncall: yes, that's the plan. chat route remains at default. we'll document thresholds in incident ticket. devon, please add note to runbook about per-route priorities.

devon: noted. adding runbook note and scheduling a revert check at +25m: ```
schedctl create --at 2026-03-15T14:55:00Z --run "rictl route update --route \"/v1/embeddings\" --region us-west-2 --limit 1400req/s --burst 800"
```

jordan_pm: contacting support to surface affected customers. initial list: three paid accounts and two trial tenants saw latency; no data loss reported. drafting customer-facing note: "We experienced degraded embeddings & rerank performance in us-west-2; temporary limits and a feature flag change have been applied to stabilize the service. We'll monitor and update within 30 minutes."

maya_oncall: prepping handoff to devon in 8 minutes. leaving checklist: commands run (route updates, key throttles, flag flip), metrics targets for rollback (p95 embeddings <500ms, 5xx rate <1%), and escalation contacts.

devon: taking active monitor duty. I'll alert if metrics regress or if more keys breach limits.

sam: post-incident follow-ups to include: 1) define per-route default caps (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) so we can avoid global defaults causing chat impacts, 2) implement adaptive per-key throttling when a tenant exceeds baseline by Xx, 3) add finer-grained telemetry for rerank batch size and latency per batch.

maya_oncall: agreed. I'll add these to the postmortem action items and assign owners. nice quick work team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied (route quotas, key throttles, feature flag). status: stabilizing. owners: devon (monitor), maya_oncall (incident coordinator), jordan_pm (customer comms).
